summary: Cook County ladder lookout near the Gunflint Trail that stopped operating around 1960; the tower is gone, and only a cab and cabin foundation remain on a BWCA trail.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Left open in the story: a BWCA site says the tower was built in the late 1930s, but a 1934 survey note already names it. The story gives both and treats 1934 as the earliest dated record.

sources.title: Smoke On the Horizon: How Fire Towers Changed BWCA History

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict: BWCAwild says built in the late 1930s, while the 1934 Cook County survey note already names the tower; the story reports both. Cab shape conflicts: the kjackson photo caption says hexagonal, the Cook County survey says octagonal remnants; the story does not name a shape. Owner is unresolved: the Cook County survey table lists Mn MFS for Gunflint, while Timberjay describes the Forest Service building the area's towers; the story and facts leave the owner out. Staffing: the Kerfoot memoir quoted on kjackson.us is undated; the November 1938 CCC newsletter is the only dated staffing item. A Facebook post by Chik-Wauk says Ken Lind worked the Gunflint tower for the Forest Service in 1947; it was not readable through fetch_text, so it is not used. Nothing found on the removal date, the tower's fate after 1966, or any notable fires. The brief's access 'unknown' is set to public because the site is reached by a hiking trail in the wilderness. Photo candidates not added (no license check).
